title: Electron Quick Guide
description: Find a short explanation and a worked example for each idea in the Electron course.

entries.name: Know the two main sides
entries.summary: Electron's main process manages desktop windows.

example.code:
Main process: creates and manages windows.
Renderer process: displays HTML, CSS and page JavaScript.
Preload script: exposes a small approved bridge between them.

entries.name: Create a local window
entries.summary: BrowserWindow creates a desktop window. Wait for app readiness before creating it, then load a local page.

entries.name: Build the renderer page
entries.summary: The renderer can use normal HTML, CSS and browser JavaScript.

example.code: Reading club

entries.name: Set a restrictive page policy
entries.summary: A Content Security Policy limits where a page can load and run content.

example.code:
<meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy" content="default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data:">
<!-- Put this in index.html head; use local external JS and CSS files. -->

entries.name: Configure a preload file
entries.summary: A preload script runs before the page and can expose a small API.

entries.name: Expose one harmless value
entries.summary: contextBridge can expose a chosen value to the renderer without sharing full Node tools.

entries.name: Ask the main process a narrow question
entries.summary: IPC lets the renderer ask the main process for an approved result.

entries.name: Handle a bridge failure
entries.summary: A request through the bridge can reject.

entries.name: Prevent unexpected navigation
entries.summary: A local app window should not become an unrestricted browser for unknown content.

entries.name: Keep a window reference
entries.summary: The main process can keep a reference to its window and clear it when the window is closed.

entries.name: Respect desktop lifecycle rules
entries.summary: Desktop platforms have different conventions after all windows close.

entries.name: Check the packaged app
entries.summary: A packaged desktop app can behave differently from the development folder.

example.code:
Use a maintained Electron packaging tool such as Electron Forge.
Build for a supported target platform.
Open the packaged app.
Check local images and scripts.
Test bridge success and failure.
Confirm no renderer Node access or unexpected new windows.
